column1: # Known startup dialogs, and the configuration entry that resolves each.
# A newly launched session can be held before it reads anything, by a dialog
# that expects a person. This table lets the launcher say WHICH dialog, and
# what settles it, instead of reporting a bare timeout.
# It is a diagnostic table, not an answering machine. Nothing here is ever
# typed at a dialog: every entry is resolved by recording a decision in
# configuration, deliberately, in advance. Simulating a keypress at a security
# prompt would mean this tool answering a question that was asked of a person,
# and the option order, highlight glyph, input timing and even the control
# type all vary by version and terminal — so a scripted answer is not only
# presumptuous, it is unreliable, and its failure mode is answering "no" while
# reporting that the session never started.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   id       short name, used in reports
#   pattern  a literal string that appears in the pane when the dialog shows
#   what     one line describing what is being asked
#   remedy   what to do about it
# Patterns are matched literally, not as expressions, so a stray character in
# a dialog cannot turn into a wildcard. Blank lines and lines starting with #
# are ignored. Order matters: the first match wins, so put the more specific
# dialogs above the more general ones.
# Verified against CLI 2.1.259.
trust
column3: The workspace has not been trusted yet, so the session is asking before it will read or run anything here.
column4: Re-run with --trust-folder, which records trust for this workspace before launching. Or start the CLI in this directory once by hand and accept the prompt.

column1: bypass-disclaimer
column3: Permissions were bypassed for this session, and the disclaimer covering that has not been accepted on this machine yet.
column4: Run the CLI once interactively with permissions bypassed and accept the disclaimer. It is recorded per machine, not per session, so this is needed once.

column1: settings-trust
column3: The directory carries project settings the session has not been authorised to load.
column4: Start the CLI here once by hand and accept, after reading what the settings do.

column1: mcp-server-trust
column3: The directory declares external servers that have not been approved.
column4: Start the CLI here once by hand and approve the servers you intend to use.

column1: external-includes
column3: Project instructions reference files outside the workspace, and loading them has not been approved.
column4: Start the CLI here once by hand and accept, after checking what is being included.

column1: onboarding
column3: First-run setup has not been completed for this machine; it runs before anything else.
column4: Run the CLI once interactively and complete first-run setup.
